clue.text: Lionesses frolicking without making a sound

indicators.note: frolicking means romping about, so the letters of lionesses are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pride of lionesses play-fighting in total silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolicking' rearranges the nine letters of LIONESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done silently produces no noise at all, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Scoffed a lot about a cigarette-end

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: the end of the word cigarette is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone bingeing while chatting over a cigarette stub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' takes the last letter of 'cigarette', E, after OVER and A; 'cigarette-end' looks like one stub but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffing a lot means eating to excess.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment with splash-back set in place

indicators.note: set in tells us one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a spot is a place

indicators.note: back tells us the word for splash is written from right to left

parts.note: to splash something is to wet it

explanation.surface: Fitting a splashback behind the cooker in a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns WET into TEW, and 'set in' puts it inside SPOT: S-TEW-POT. 'Splash-back' looks like the kitchen tiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep cooking pot used for stews is a standard item of kitchenware.

clue.text: Hide the contents of study

definitions.note: hide used as an adjective, as in hide boots, made of animal skin

indicators.note: contents of says the first word sits inside the word for study

parts.note: to learn is to study

explanation.surface: Concealing what is in a study or den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of' places THE inside LEARN. 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the attributive noun, meaning made of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective for goods made from tanned animal skin, like a strap or flask.

clue.text: Soppy eccentric occupying nurse

indicators.note: occupying means filling the space inside the word for nurse

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
odd means eccentric

explanation.surface: A sentimental oddball moving in on a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse, an old British nursing grade) has ODD inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppy here means soaking wet, as in ground thoroughly drenched by rain.

clue.text: The theatre-worker had agents in revolt

indicators.note: in revolt suggests overturning, so the letters of had agents are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A stage worker whose agents rose up against him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolt' rearranges HADAGENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstage employee who shifts scenery and props during a play.

clue.text: A fellow giving a poor actor housing support

indicators.note: housing means holding another word inside, here between the two parts

parts.note: a ham is an overacting, poor performer
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A man handing an untalented performer some supportive help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' puts BRA inside A HAM, splitting it as A-BRA-HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, and the biblical patriarch, so any bloke with that name.

clue.text: Notes sound increase

parts.note: read as music: a passage where the notes grow steadily louder

explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for a gradual rise in volume over a passage.

clue.text: A month in Medoc to be remembered

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Bordeaux wine trip to recall one autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: The month runs through 'Medoc to be remembered'; Medoc is a Bordeaux wine region.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the calendar year.

clue.text: No particular top man

explanation.surface: Not any specific boss.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means broad, not specific; as a noun, a high-ranking army officer.

clue.text: A hot time at Cruft's?

parts.note: Cruft's is a famous British dog show, so a hot spell there is jokingly named for its canine entrants

explanation.definitionFit: The sultriest weeks of summer, traditionally linked with the rising of the Dog Star.

clue.text: This will give light cover

parts.note: the light is a lamp, and the item covers it rather than being a light covering

explanation.definitionFit: A shade fitted over a bulb to soften and direct its glow.

clue.text: See this as a bishop's responsibility

definitions.text: See this as a bishop's responsibility

parts.words: See this as a bishop's responsibility
parts.note: see is the noun for a bishop's area, not the verb of looking

explanation.definitionFit: The district under a bishop's authority, also called a see.

clue.text: Hate coin production that's rudimentary

indicators.note: production suggests making something new, so the letters of hate coin are reshaped

explanation.surface: Minting coins that nobody likes, all very primitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges HATECOIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just begun and not yet developed is undeveloped or basic.

clue.text: Harry, the Trojan hero

explanation.surface: Prince Harry cast as a Greek-legend warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to bully or badger; also Priam's son, Troy's champion, killed by Achilles.

clue.text: Music-maker-a choir-man possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of a choir-man may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps a singer in a choir is also a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ACHOIRMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is a small instrument played by blowing.

clue.text: Shop in the open air with healthier result

parts.note: out means outdoors, as in eating out in the garden
fitter means in better health

explanation.surface: Getting outside in the fresh air leaves you in better shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothing retailer, or the business that kits people out.

clue.text: The white horse fancied with point

definitions.text: The white horse fancied with point

parts.words: The white horse fancied with point
parts.note: a pale steed that exists only in imagination, bearing a single sharp horn on its brow

explanation.definitionFit: A mythical beast, horse-like with one spiralling horn.

clue.text: Left after the party-went first in some confusion

indicators.note: after tells us the abbreviation for left follows the party word

parts.note: a rave is a lively party
to have led is to have gone first

explanation.surface: Someone left after a party where they had led the way, rather muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: RAVE, then L placed 'after' it, then LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled or snarled, like knotted threads.

clue.text: The novel "Dieting", a journalist's work

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of dieting are made anew

explanation.surface: A reporter writing a book called Dieting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book title's label but rearranges DIETING.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparing copy for publication is a large part of newspaper work.

clue.text: A serving man gets into trouble when slow

indicators.note: gets into means the serving man is placed inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
GI is an American soldier, a serviceman

explanation.surface: A soldier in hot water when he is too slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets into' puts A GI inside ADO: AD-AGI-O.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning at a leisurely tempo.

clue.text: A girl about ten feels for a six-footer

indicators.note: about here means surrounding the number

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman of ten reaching out to a very tall man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps ANNA round TEN. A six-footer is an insect, with six legs, not a tall person.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's feeler, its sensory organ for touch.

clue.text: Set apart, and that is nothing new

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
late can mean recent, as in the late news

explanation.surface: Separated, but that is hardly news.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate or keep away from others.

clue.text: The doctor is fed maybe about one and changes

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the numeral
maybe signals the letters of is fed are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor, perhaps fed by others, keeps altering things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns ISFED into DIFES, and 'about' wraps it round I to give DIFIES after MO.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify is to alter, so the verb fits the third person.

clue.text: Revolutionary movements

parts.note: not political uprisings but water turning in circles

explanation.definitionFit: Small whirlpools are currents circling round.

clue.text: Keeping it need not appear wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of it need not are out of their right order

explanation.surface: It need not seem wrong to hold on to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ITNEEDNOT; 'appear' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding someone in custody, as at a school after hours.

clue.text: Honoured all round at having written some music

indicators.note: all round says the first word encloses the second

parts.note: noted means famous, distinguished

explanation.surface: A composer honoured on every side for their score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' places AT inside NOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Music set down in written symbols on a score.

clue.text: Pretend not to know of club without affiliation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the club word goes round the other

parts.note: a bat is a club for striking a ball
a link is a connection or affiliation

explanation.surface: Joining a sports club as an independent member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: BAT goes round LINK.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something by deliberately overlooking it.

clue.text: Once daughter enters the Church give up

indicators.note: enters means going inside the abbreviation for the Church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Once a daughter is in the church, she surrenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts ONCE and D inside CE (Church of England).
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or admit defeat.

clue.text: With little money in spare change? That's rough!

indicators.note: in says the pieces sit inside the rearranged letters
change suggests the letters of spare are altered in order

parts.note: and can mean with, as in fish and chips
P is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Short of cash in your spare change? Tough luck!
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges SPARE to S...APER and 'in' puts AND and P (penny) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasive paper, coarse to the touch, used for smoothing wood.
